16: # Devin CLI - Complete Command Reference
17: 
18: Comprehensive reference for all Devin CLI commands, flags, models, configuration, and troubleshooting.
19: 
20: ---
21: 
22: ## 1. OVERVIEW
23: 
24: ### Core Principle
25: 
26: Devin CLI is Cognition's terminal-based AI coding agent — a fast, minimal agent that lives both in the terminal and in the cloud. It fronts a broad multi-model surface; this skill curates seven families in scope — DeepSeek, Gemini, GLM-5.2, GPT-5.6 (Luna Max), GPT-6 (Luna Max), Grok (4.5 and 4.6), and SWE-2 (full catalog: [providers-and-models.md](./providers-and-models.md)). Devin's native Adaptive model router and its full 48-family roster remain available via `devin models list` but are out of this skill's curated scope. The skill dispatches `swe` (alias → `swe-2`) at `accept-edits` permission mode by default; users can override the model and mode. It provides direct access to multi-model coding, subagent delegation, cloud handoff, MCP integration, and session management — all governed by configurable permission modes.
27: 
28: ### Purpose
29: 
30: Provide a comprehensive, single-source reference for all Devin CLI commands, flags, models, configuration options, permission modes, and troubleshooting guidance.
31: 
32: ### When to Use
33: 
34: - Setting up or configuring Devin CLI
35: - Looking up command-line flags, subcommands, or permission modes
36: - Troubleshooting authentication, sandbox, or session issues
37: - Configuring subagents via `.devin/agents/[name]/AGENT.md`
38: - Selecting the right permission mode for a task
39: 
40: ### Key Sources
41: 
42: | Source | URL |
43: |--------|-----|
44: | **Documentation** | https://docs.devin.ai/cli |
45: | **Web App** | https://app.devin.ai |
46: | **Runtime** | Node.js / native binary |
47: | **Version** | 3000.2.17 |
48: 
49: ---
50: 
51: ## 2. INSTALLATION
52: 
53: | Method | Command | Notes |
54: |--------|---------|-------|
55: | **Interactive setup** | `devin setup` | Wizard for auth + MCP configuration |
56: | **Direct install** | `curl -fsSL https://devin.ai/install \| bash` | Persistent install |
57: | **Update** | `devin update` | Check for and install updates |
58: | **Force update** | `devin update --force` | Re-install even if on latest version |
59: 
60: **Platform support:**
61: 
62: | Platform | Status |
63: |----------|--------|
64: | macOS | Full support (sandbox via Seatbelt, works out of the box) |
65: | Linux | Full support (sandbox requires `bwrap` + `socat`) |
66: | Windows (WSL) | Use WSL 2; native Windows cannot run the sandbox |
67: 
68: After installation, run `devin` for the interactive REPL or `devin -p -- "prompt"` for non-interactive use.
69: 
70: ---
71: 
72: ## 3. AUTHENTICATION
73: 
74: cli-devin authenticates through **Devin account OAuth only** — `devin auth login` (browser flow). It does not use an API key.
75: 
76: **OAuth login/logout:**
77: 
78: ```bash
79: # Authenticate via Devin account (opens browser)
80: devin auth login
81: 
82: # For SSH/remote sessions (skip browser, manually paste token)
83: devin auth login --force-manual-token-flow
84: 
85: # View authentication status
86: devin auth status
87: 
88: # Log out and clear stored credentials
89: devin auth logout
90: ```
91: 
92: **Auth status output:**
93: 
94: ```
95: Logged in (via Devin).
96: 
97: Credentials:
98:   File:              ~/.local/share/devin/credentials.toml
99:   API server:        https://server.codeium.com
100:   Devin webapp:      https://app.devin.ai
101:   Devin API:         https://api.devin.ai
102: ```
103: 
104: ---
105: 
106: ## 4. COMMAND-LINE FLAGS
107: 
108: ### Essential Flags
109: 
110: | Flag | Short | Values | Description |
111: |------|-------|--------|-------------|
112: | `--model` | | `<model-name>` | Model to use — `swe` (default alias → `swe-2`), plus the curated DeepSeek / GLM-5.2 / GPT-5.6 Luna Max / GPT-6 Luna Max / Grok (4.5 and 4.6) / SWE-2 families (see §5) |
113: | `--permission-mode` | | canonical: `normal`, `accept-edits`, `smart`, `dangerous`, `autonomous` — aliases: `auto`→`normal`, `yolo`/`bypass`→`dangerous` | Permission mode controlling tool auto-approval. **`devin --help` prints only 4 of these 8 accepted values** — it is not the authoritative enum. See the probe below. |
114: | `--print` | `-p` | `[<prompt>]` | Non-interactive mode: print response and exit |
115: | `--continue` | `-c` | (none) | Continue the most recent session in the current directory |
116: | `--resume` | `-r` | `[<session-id>]` | Resume a specific session by ID, or select interactively |
117: | `--sandbox` | | (none) | Enable OS-level process sandboxing (selects `autonomous` permission mode) |
118: | `--prompt-file` | | `<file>` | Load the initial prompt from a file |
119: 
120: > **Verifying a flag value without spending a session.** `--help` under-reports the
121: > `--permission-mode` enum, so never conclude a value is invalid because help omits it.
122: > Force parse-time validation instead: an invalid value fails at exit 2 before the file
123: > is read, a valid one reaches the file error at exit 1.
124: >
125: > ```bash
126: > devin --permission-mode <value> --prompt-file /nonexistent
127: > #   exit 2 + "invalid value ..."        -> rejected by the binary
128: > #   exit 1 + "Failed to read prompt file" -> accepted
129: > ```
130: >
131: > Verified against `devin 3000.6.7`: `auto`, `normal`, `accept-edits`, `smart`,
132: > `dangerous`, `yolo`, `bypass`, `autonomous` all accepted; `plan` and `manual`
133: > (Claude's modes, not Devin's) rejected. Re-run the probe after a CLI upgrade —
134: > `smart` was rejected at 3000.2.17 and is accepted at 3000.6.7.
135: | `--config` | | `<path>` | Configuration file path (override default `~/.config/devin/config.json`) |
136: | `--export` | | `[<path>]` | Export conversation to a file after each turn (ATIF format) |
137: | `--agent-config` | | `<file>` | Declarative agent configuration file (JSON or YAML) |
138: | `--respect-workspace-trust` | | `true`, `false` | Respect workspace trust settings |
139: 
140: ### Prompt Syntax
141: 
142: ```bash
143: # Interactive REPL (no prompt)
144: devin
145: 
146: # Start REPL with initial prompt (use -- before the prompt)
147: devin -- your prompt here
148: 
149: # Non-interactive: print mode
150: devin -p -- "prompt"
151: devin -p -- "prompt words here"    # Same, using -- separator
152: ```
153: 
154: ### Permission Mode Values
155: 
156: | Value | Behavior | Best For |
157: |-------|----------|----------|
158: | `auto` | Auto-approves read-only tools; prompts for writes and shell | Review, analysis, research |
159: | `accept-edits` | Auto-approves workspace edits + read-only; prompts for shell | Code generation, bug fixing, documentation |
160: | `smart` | Auto-runs actions a fast model judges safe | Trusted workflows with judgment calls |
161: | `dangerous` | Auto-approves all tools without prompting | Full trust — **requires explicit user approval** |
162: | `autonomous` | Sandbox-enforced; only available with `--sandbox` | Unattended execution with OS-level limits |
163: 
164: ### Usage Examples
165: 
166: ```bash
167: # Interactive REPL
168: devin
169: 
170: # Non-interactive with model selection
171: devin -p --model gpt-5-6-luna-max -- "Refactor utils.ts to use async/await"
172: 
173: # With permission mode for file edits
174: devin -p --permission-mode accept-edits -- "Add error handling to auth.ts"
175: 
176: # Continue the most recent session
177: devin -c
178: 
179: # Resume a specific session
180: devin -r brisk-otter
181: 
182: # With OS-level sandbox
183: devin --sandbox -p -- "Run the test suite and fix failures"
184: 
185: # Load prompt from file
186: devin -p --prompt-file ./prompt.txt
187: 
188: # Export conversation
189: devin --export out.json -- fix the tests
190: 
191: # Start REPL with initial prompt
192: devin -- add a login page
193: ```
194: 
195: ---
196: 
197: ## 5. MODEL SELECTION
198: 
199: ### Supported Models
200: 
201: Devin dispatches **`swe`** (alias → `swe-2`) at the **`accept-edits`** permission mode by default. The model is switched per-dispatch with `--model <alias>` (short names resolve to the latest version in that family). There is no headless reasoning-effort flag — depth is expressed through the permission mode (autonomy) and the chosen model, not a reasoning flag; interactive REPL sessions cycle thinking depth with `Alt+T` (macOS: `Opt+T`).
202: 
203: **Full curated roster (DeepSeek / Gemini / GLM-5.2 / GPT-5.6 Luna Max / SWE-2 families) → [providers-and-models.md](./providers-and-models.md).** Devin's native Adaptive router and full 48-family roster are out of this skill's curated scope.
204: 
205: ### Setting the Model
206: 
207: ```bash
208: # Command flag
209: devin --model gpt-5-6-luna-max -- refactor this module
210: devin --model glm-5-2 -- explain this code
211: devin -p --model swe -- "list all TODO comments"
212: 
213: # Slash command (inside REPL)
214: /model gpt-5-6-luna-max
215: /model glm-5-2
216: /model deepseek-v4-flash-max
217: 
218: # Config file (~/.config/devin/config.json)
219: {
220:   "agent": {
221:     "model": "swe"
222:   }
223: }
224: ```
225: 
226: ### Selection Strategy
227: 
228: | Task Type | Model | Rationale |
229: |-----------|-------|-----------|
230: | Architecture decisions | `gpt-5-6-luna-max` | Multi-faceted analysis benefits from deep reasoning |
231: | Security audits | `gpt-5-6-luna-max` | Catches subtle vulnerability patterns |
232: | Complex planning | `gpt-5-6-luna-max` / `glm-5-2-max` | Multi-strategy evaluation benefits from depth |
233: | Code generation | `glm-5-2` / `glm-5-2-max` | Balanced for most generation tasks |
234: | Standard code review | `glm-5-2` / `swe-2-high` | Efficient for pattern-based review |
235: | Implementation | `glm-5-2` / `swe-2-high` | Balanced for translating specs to code |
236: | Test generation | `swe-2-high` / `glm-5-2` | Solid test structure output |
237: | Documentation | `glm-5-2` / `swe` | Efficient for structured doc generation |
238: | Quick edits / lookups | `swe-2-medium` | Lowest-effort SWE-2 tier, free |
239: | Lowest latency, cost accepted | `swe-1-7-lightning` | The only lightning tier; metered, not free |
240: | Cost-sensitive work | `swe` / `swe-2-medium` | SWE-2 is free across all three effort tiers |
241: 
242: Always specify `--model` explicitly in scripts for predictability; omitting it relies on the CLI default from `~/.config/devin/config.json`, which may differ across machines.
243: 
244: ---
245: 
246: ## 6. OUTPUT HANDLING
247: 
248: ### Print Mode Output
249: 
250: `devin -p` writes its output to stdout. Use shell redirection or command substitution to capture it.
251: 
252: ```bash
253: # Capture to file
254: devin -p \
255:   --model swe \
256:   -- \
257:   "Generate a TypeScript interface for the User model" > /tmp/user-interface.ts
258: 
259: # Capture to variable
260: RESULT=$(devin -p --model swe -- "List all exported functions in src/")
261: echo "$RESULT"
262: 
263: # Pipe to another command
264: devin -p --model swe -- "Generate SQL schema for users table" | psql -d mydb -f -
265: 
266: # Redirect stderr separately
267: devin -p --model swe -- "Analyze auth flow" > /tmp/analysis.txt 2>/tmp/errors.txt
268: ```
269: 
270: ### Export Format
271: 
272: Use `--export` to save the full conversation in ATIF format:
273: 
274: ```bash
275: # Export to default path
276: devin --export -- fix the tests
277: 
278: # Export to specific file
279: devin --export out.json -- fix tests
280: ```
281: 
282: ### Exit Codes
283: 
284: | Code | Meaning |
285: |------|---------|
286: | `0` | Success |
287: | Non-zero | Error (check stderr for details) |
288: 
289: ---
290: 
291: ## 7. INTERACTIVE COMMANDS
292: 
293: When running `devin` in interactive (REPL) mode, these slash commands are available:
294: 
295: ### Navigation & Control
296: 
297: | Command | Description |
298: |---------|-------------|
299: | `/help` | See all available commands |
300: | `/exit` or `/quit` | Exit the application |
301: | `/clear` or `/new` | Clear conversation history (start fresh) |
302: 
303: ### Mode Switching
304: 
305: | Command | Description |
306: |---------|-------------|
307: | `/mode` | Show current mode |
308: | `/mode <name>` | Switch mode (`normal`, `accept-edits`, `plan`, `bypass`; `autonomous` in sandbox sessions) |
309: | `/normal` | Switch to Normal mode (default) |
310: | `/accept-edits` | Switch to Accept Edits mode |
311: | `/plan` | Switch to Plan mode (read-only planning) |
312: | `/ask <question>` | Ask a question without making code changes (oneshot) |
313: | `/bypass` | Switch to Bypass mode (aliases: `/yolo`, `/dangerous`) |
314: 
315: ### Model Switching
316: 
317: | Command | Description |
318: |---------|-------------|
319: | `/model` | Show model selector |
320: | `/model <name>` | Switch to a specific model |
321: | `/fast` | Switch to SWE-1.6 Fast |
322: 
323: ### Session Management
324: 
325: | Command | Description |
326: |---------|-------------|
327: | `/resume` | Open the interactive session picker |
328: | `/resume <id>` | Resume session by ID |
329: | `/continue [id]` | Resume most recent or specific session |
330: | `/fork [step]` | Fork the current session to a new session |
331: | `/steps` | List conversation steps (use with `/fork` and `/revert`) |
332: | `/revert <step>` | Revert file changes from a specific step onwards |
333: | `/ls [--all]` | List recent sessions (current directory only by default) |
334: | `/rm-session <id>` | Irreversibly delete a session |
335: | `/rename-session <title>` | Rename the current session |
336: 
337: ### Cloud Sessions
338: 
339: | Command | Description |
340: |---------|-------------|
341: | `/handoff [task]` | Hand off the current session to a cloud Devin session |
342: | `/cloud-sessions [--all]` | Open interactive picker of recent cloud sessions |
343: | `/cloud-attach <id>` | Attach to a cloud Devin session with full TUI |
344: 
345: ### Workspace
346: 
347: | Command | Description |
348: |---------|-------------|
349: | `/workspace` | List workspace directories |
350: | `/add-dir <path>` | Add additional workspace directory |
351: | `/undo-add-dir <path>` | Remove a workspace directory |
352: 
353: ### Automation
354: 
355: | Command | Description |
356: |---------|-------------|
357: | `/loop <prompt>` | Run a prompt then auto-review the diff in a loop |
358: 
359: ### Utilities
360: 
361: | Command | Description |
362: |---------|-------------|
363: | `/context` | Show context window usage |
364: | `/usage` | Show estimated credit/ACU usage for the session |
365: | `/compact` | Force conversation compaction |
366: | `/login` | Authenticate with your account |
367: | `/logout` | Clear stored credentials and exit |
368: | `/update [--force]` | Check for and install updates |
369: | `/hooks` | List all loaded hooks |
370: 
371: ---
372: 
373: ## 8. SPECIAL INPUT SYNTAX
374: 
375: ### File References
376: 
377: Use `@` in the REPL to open autocomplete for local files/directories. Selected files are added as context.
378: 
379: ```bash
380: # In the REPL, type:
381: @src/utils.ts refactor this to use the repository pattern
382: ```
383: 
384: ### Image Input
385: 
386: Paste images from your clipboard with `Ctrl+V`. Attached images appear in the input area and can be managed with `Left/Right` to navigate and `Backspace` to remove.
387: 
388: ### Shell Integration
389: 
390: ```bash
391: # Pass git diff as context
392: git diff HEAD~1 | devin -p --model swe -- "Summarize these changes"
393: 
394: # Combine file content with prompt
395: cat src/auth.ts | devin -p --model swe -- "Add input validation to all functions"
396: ```
397: 
398: ---
399: 
400: ## 9. CONFIGURATION FILES
401: 
402: ### Directory Structure
403: 
404: ```
405: .devin/
406: ├── config.json          # Project-level CLI configuration
407: ├── config.local.json    # Local override (not shared with team)
408: ├── hooks/               # Lifecycle hooks
409: └── agents/
410:     └── [name]/
411:         └── AGENT.md     # Custom subagent profile
412: ```
413: 
414: ### config.json Format
415: 
416: ```json
417: // .devin/config.json or ~/.config/devin/config.json
418: {
419:   "agent": {
420:     "model": "swe"
421:   },
422:   "permissions": {
423:     "allow": [
424:       "Read(src/**)",
425:       "Write(src/**)",
426:       "Exec(git)",
427:       "Exec(npm run)"
428:     ],
429:     "deny": [
430:       "Exec(rm -rf)",
431:       "Exec(sudo)"
432:     ]
433:   },
434:   "mcpServers": {
435:     "my-server": {
436:       "command": "npx",
437:       "args": ["@company/mcp-server"],
438:       "transport": "stdio"
439:     }
440:   }
441: }
442: ```
443: 
444: ### Permission Syntax
445: 
446: **Scope-based:**
447: 
448: | Matcher | Controls | Example |
449: |---------|----------|---------|
450: | `Read(glob)` | File read access | `Read(src/**)` |
451: | `Write(glob)` | File write access | `Write(src/**)` |
452: | `Exec(prefix)` | Shell command execution | `Exec(git)`, `Exec(npm run)` |
453: | `Fetch(pattern)` | HTTP fetch access | `Fetch(https://api.github.com/*)` |
454: 
455: **Tool-based:** `read`, `edit`, `grep`, `glob`, `exec`
456: 
457: **MCP tool-based:** `mcp__server__tool`, `mcp__server__*`, `mcp__*`
458: 
459: ### Permission Precedence
460: 
461: 1. Organization/team settings (if enterprise) — highest
462: 2. Session-level grants (interactive approvals)
463: 3. Project local config (`.devin/config.local.json`)
464: 4. Project config (`.devin/config.json`)
465: 5. User config (`~/.config/devin/config.json`) — lowest
466: 
467: Deny is checked before ask, and ask is checked before allow. A deny rule always wins.
468: 
469: ---
470: 
471: ## 10. PERMISSION MODES
472: 
473: Permission modes control what the agent can do without asking for approval. Always choose the least-permissive mode that allows the task to complete.
474: 
475: ### Mode Reference
476: 
477: | Mode | Flag | Read-only | Fetch | Bash | File edits | Use Case |
478: |------|------|-----------|-------|------|------------|----------|
479: | **Auto** | `auto` | Auto | Prompt | Prompt | Prompt | Analysis, review, exploration |
480: | **Accept Edits** | `accept-edits` | Auto | Prompt | Prompt | Auto (workspace) | Code generation, refactoring |
481: | **Smart** | `smart` | Auto | Safe actions | Safe actions | Auto (workspace) | Trusted workflows with judgment |
482: | **Dangerous** | `dangerous` | Auto | Auto | Auto | Auto | Full trust — **requires explicit approval** |
483: | **Autonomous** | `autonomous` (+ `--sandbox`) | Auto | Auto (sandbox) | Auto (sandbox) | Prompt (edit/write tools bypass sandbox) | Unattended execution with OS limits |
484: 
485: ### Safety Guidance
486: 
487: ```bash
488: # SAFE: Auto mode for analysis
489: devin -p --permission-mode auto --model swe -- "Map the authentication flow"
490: 
491: # STANDARD: Accept Edits for code changes
492: devin -p --permission-mode accept-edits --model swe -- "Add error handling to all API routes"
493: 
494: # ELEVATED RISK: Dangerous mode — use only with explicit approval
495: devin -p --permission-mode dangerous --model gpt-5-6-luna-max -- "Migrate database schema"
496: 
497: # AUTONOMOUS: OS-enforced sandbox
498: devin --sandbox -p --model swe -- "Run the test suite and fix failures"
499: ```
500: 
501: ### Bypass vs Autonomous
502: 
503: | | Bypass (`dangerous`) | Autonomous (`--sandbox`) |
504: |---|---|---|
505: | Requires `--sandbox` | No | Yes (only available in sandbox sessions) |
506: | Shell commands | Auto-approved, unrestricted | Auto-approved, contained by sandbox |
507: | File writes via edit/write tools | Auto-approved anywhere | Still prompt (granting a scope expands the sandbox) |
508: | Network access | Unrestricted | Filtered by sandbox domain allow/deny lists |
509: | Respects admin Team Settings | Yes | Yes |
510: 
511: Pick `dangerous` when you trust the agent with your whole machine. Pick `--sandbox` (autonomous) when you want unattended execution with OS-enforced limits.
512: 
513: ---
514: 
515: ## 11. SESSION MANAGEMENT
516: 
517: ### Session Subcommands
518: 
519: | Subcommand | Description |
520: |------------|-------------|
521: | `devin` | Launch REPL; session picker available |
522: | `devin -c` | Continue the most recent session in the current directory |
523: | `devin -r` | Resume — pick from recent sessions interactively |
524: | `devin -r <session-id>` | Resume a specific session by ID |
525: | `devin list` | List sessions in the current directory (alias: `devin ls`) |
526: | `devin list --format json` | Output sessions as JSON |
527: | `devin list --format csv` | Output sessions as CSV |
528: 
529: ### Session Picker
530: 
531: Running `devin` without arguments opens the REPL. Use `/resume` inside the REPL to open the interactive session picker, or `/continue` to resume the most recent session.
532: 
533: ### Scripted Session Resume
534: 
535: ```bash
536: # Continue the most recent session non-interactively
537: devin -c -p "Continue implementing the rate limiter" --model swe
538: 
539: # Resume a specific session
540: devin -r brisk-otter -p "Continue from where we left off" --model swe
541: 
542: # List sessions as JSON for scripting
543: devin list --format json
544: ```
545: 
546: ### When to Use Each Operation
547: 
548: | Operation | When to Use |
549: |-----------|-------------|
550: | `-c` / `--continue` | Continue the most recent session with existing context |
551: | `-r` / `--resume` | Resume a specific session by ID |
552: | `/fork` | Fork the current session to try a different approach |
553: | `/revert` | Revert file changes from a specific step and rewind conversation |
554: | New session | Fresh context; previous session is not relevant |
555: | `-p` (stateless) | One-shot tasks; simpler to re-provide context than manage sessions |
556: 
557: ---
558: 
559: ## 12. SUBCOMMANDS
560: 
561: | Subcommand | Description |
562: |------------|-------------|
563: | `devin auth` | Authentication (login, logout, status) |
564: | `devin mcp` | MCP server management (add, list, get, remove, login, logout, enable, disable) |
565: | `devin models` | List available models organized by family |
566: | `devin rules` | Manage agent rules (always-on context blobs) |
567: | `devin skills` | Manage agent skills (slash commands and context blobs) |
568: | `devin plugins` | Manage plugins (install, list, info, update, remove) |
569: | `devin cloud` | Manage Devin Cloud resources (DRS: environment blueprints, sandbox sessions, builds) |
570: | `devin list` | List sessions in the current directory (alias: `ls`) |
571: | `devin update` | Check for and optionally install updates |
572: | `devin version` | Print the current version |
573: | `devin migrate` | Migrate configuration from other tools |
574: | `devin sandbox` | Process sandboxing for the exec tool (research preview) |
575: | `devin setup` | Interactive setup wizard |
576: | `devin uninstall` | Uninstall and remove data |
577: | `devin acp` | Run as an ACP (Agent Client Protocol) server over stdio |
578: | `devin shell` | Shell integration (init, run, setup) |
579: 
580: ---
581: 
582: ## 13. TROUBLESHOOTING
583: 
584: | Problem | Cause | Solution |
585: |---------|-------|----------|
586: | `not authenticated` / auth error | Devin account OAuth not configured | Run `devin auth login` (browser flow) |
587: | `Authentication failed` | OAuth session expired or invalid | Re-run `devin auth login` to re-authenticate |
588: | `Command not found: devin` | Not installed or not in PATH | Run `devin setup` or `curl -fsSL https://devin.ai/install \| bash`; verify with `which devin` |
589: | Task ran but no files changed | `devin -p` defaulted to `auto` (read-only) | Add `--permission-mode accept-edits` or `dangerous` |
590: | Session resume fails | Session ID invalid or expired | List sessions via `devin list`; start a new session |
591: | Slow response | Large context or complex task | Break task into smaller steps; use `auto` for analysis; use `swe-2-medium` for quick lookups, or `swe-1-7-lightning` when latency matters more than cost |
592: | `--sandbox` fails to start | Platform prerequisites missing | Run `devin sandbox setup` (Linux needs `bwrap` + `socat`; macOS works out of the box) |
593: | Cloud handoff fails | Network issue or uncommitted changes blocking | Commit or stash unwanted changes; verify connectivity to `app.devin.ai` |
594: | Subagent denied tools | Background subagent cannot prompt for permissions | Resume the subagent in the foreground to approve tools |
595: | MCP server not responding | Server not running or misconfigured | Check `devin mcp list`; verify server config in `.devin/config.json` |
596: | Windows compatibility | WSL not configured | Use WSL 2; native Windows cannot run the sandbox |
597: 
598: ---
599: 
600: ## 14. ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES
601: 
602: | Variable | Purpose | Example |
603: |----------|---------|---------|
604: | `DEVIN_MODEL` | Default model override | `swe`, `glm-5-2`, `gpt-5-6-luna-max` |
605: | `DEVIN_PERMISSION_MODE` | Default permission mode | `auto`, `accept-edits`, `smart`, `dangerous` |
606: | `DEVIN_SANDBOX` | Enable sandbox | `1` |
607: | `DEVIN_PROJECT_DIR` | Project root directory (set automatically by Devin on session start) | `/path/to/project` |
608: | `WINDSURF_API_KEY` | ACP server credentials (alternative to stored auth) | API key string |

16: # Devin CLI - Complete Command Reference
17: 
18: Comprehensive reference for all Devin CLI commands, flags, models, configuration, and troubleshooting.
19: 
20: ---
21: 
22: ## 1. OVERVIEW
23: 
24: ### Core Principle
25: 
26: Devin CLI is Cognition's terminal-based AI coding agent — a fast, minimal agent that lives both in the terminal and in the cloud. It fronts a broad multi-model surface; this skill curates seven families in scope — DeepSeek, Gemini, GLM-5.2, GPT-5.6 (Luna Max), GPT-6 (Luna Max), Grok (4.5 and 4.6), and SWE-2 (full catalog: [providers-and-models.md](./providers-and-models.md)). Devin's native Adaptive model router and its full 48-family roster remain available via `devin models list` but are out of this skill's curated scope. The skill dispatches `swe` (alias → `swe-2`) at `accept-edits` permission mode by default; users can override the model and mode. It provides direct access to multi-model coding, subagent delegation, cloud handoff, MCP integration, and session management — all governed by configurable permission modes.
27: 
28: ### Purpose
29: 
30: Provide a comprehensive, single-source reference for all Devin CLI commands, flags, models, configuration options, permission modes, and troubleshooting guidance.
31: 
32: ### When to Use
33: 
34: - Setting up or configuring Devin CLI
35: - Looking up command-line flags, subcommands, or permission modes
36: - Troubleshooting authentication, sandbox, or session issues
37: - Configuring subagents via `.devin/agents/[name]/AGENT.md`
38: - Selecting the right permission mode for a task
39: 
40: ### Key Sources
41: 
42: | Source | URL |
43: |--------|-----|
44: | **Documentation** | https://docs.devin.ai/cli |
45: | **Web App** | https://app.devin.ai |
46: | **Runtime** | Node.js / native binary |
47: | **Version** | 3000.2.17 |
48: 
49: ---
50: 
51: ## 2. INSTALLATION
52: 
53: | Method | Command | Notes |
54: |--------|---------|-------|
55: | **Interactive setup** | `devin setup` | Wizard for auth + MCP configuration |
56: | **Direct install** | `curl -fsSL https://devin.ai/install \| bash` | Persistent install |
57: | **Update** | `devin update` | Check for and install updates |
58: | **Force update** | `devin update --force` | Re-install even if on latest version |
59: 
60: **Platform support:**
61: 
62: | Platform | Status |
63: |----------|--------|
64: | macOS | Full support (sandbox via Seatbelt, works out of the box) |
65: | Linux | Full support (sandbox requires `bwrap` + `socat`) |
66: | Windows (WSL) | Use WSL 2; native Windows cannot run the sandbox |
67: 
68: After installation, run `devin` for the interactive REPL or `devin -p -- "prompt"` for non-interactive use.
69: 
70: ---
71: 
72: ## 3. AUTHENTICATION
73: 
74: cli-devin authenticates through **Devin account OAuth only** — `devin auth login` (browser flow). It does not use an API key.
75: 
76: **OAuth login/logout:**
77: 
78: ```bash
79: # Authenticate via Devin account (opens browser)
80: devin auth login
81: 
82: # For SSH/remote sessions (skip browser, manually paste token)
83: devin auth login --force-manual-token-flow
84: 
85: # View authentication status
86: devin auth status
87: 
88: # Log out and clear stored credentials
89: devin auth logout
90: ```
91: 
92: **Auth status output:**
93: 
94: ```
95: Logged in (via Devin).
96: 
97: Credentials:
98:   File:              ~/.local/share/devin/credentials.toml
99:   API server:        https://server.codeium.com
100:   Devin webapp:      https://app.devin.ai
101:   Devin API:         https://api.devin.ai
102: ```
103: 
104: ---
105: 
106: ## 4. COMMAND-LINE FLAGS
107: 
108: ### Essential Flags
109: 
110: | Flag | Short | Values | Description |
111: |------|-------|--------|-------------|
112: | `--model` | | `<model-name>` | Model to use — `swe` (default alias → `swe-2`), plus the curated DeepSeek / GLM-5.2 / GPT-5.6 Luna Max / GPT-6 Luna Max / Grok (4.5 and 4.6) / SWE-2 families (see §5) |
113: | `--permission-mode` | | canonical: `normal`, `accept-edits`, `smart`, `dangerous`, `autonomous` — aliases: `auto`→`normal`, `yolo`/`bypass`→`dangerous` | Permission mode controlling tool auto-approval. **`devin --help` prints only 4 of these 8 accepted values** — it is not the authoritative enum. See the probe below. |
114: | `--print` | `-p` | `[<prompt>]` | Non-interactive mode: print response and exit |
115: | `--continue` | `-c` | (none) | Continue the most recent session in the current directory |
116: | `--resume` | `-r` | `[<session-id>]` | Resume a specific session by ID, or select interactively |
117: | `--sandbox` | | (none) | Enable OS-level process sandboxing (selects `autonomous` permission mode) |
118: | `--prompt-file` | | `<file>` | Load the initial prompt from a file |
119: 
120: > **Verifying a flag value without spending a session.** `--help` under-reports the
121: > `--permission-mode` enum, so never conclude a value is invalid because help omits it.
122: > Force parse-time validation instead: an invalid value fails at exit 2 before the file
123: > is read, a valid one reaches the file error at exit 1.
124: >
125: > ```bash
126: > devin --permission-mode <value> --prompt-file /nonexistent
127: > #   exit 2 + "invalid value ..."        -> rejected by the binary
128: > #   exit 1 + "Failed to read prompt file" -> accepted
129: > ```
130: >
131: > Verified against `devin 3000.6.7`: `auto`, `normal`, `accept-edits`, `smart`,
132: > `dangerous`, `yolo`, `bypass`, `autonomous` all accepted; `plan` and `manual`
133: > (Claude's modes, not Devin's) rejected. Re-run the probe after a CLI upgrade —
134: > `smart` was rejected at 3000.2.17 and is accepted at 3000.6.7.
135: | `--config` | | `<path>` | Configuration file path (override default `~/.config/devin/config.json`) |
136: | `--export` | | `[<path>]` | Export conversation to a file after each turn (ATIF format) |
137: | `--agent-config` | | `<file>` | Declarative agent configuration file (JSON or YAML) |
138: | `--respect-workspace-trust` | | `true`, `false` | Respect workspace trust settings |
139: 
140: ### Prompt Syntax
141: 
142: ```bash
143: # Interactive REPL (no prompt)
144: devin
145: 
146: # Start REPL with initial prompt (use -- before the prompt)
147: devin -- your prompt here
148: 
149: # Non-interactive: print mode
150: devin -p -- "prompt"
151: devin -p -- "prompt words here"    # Same, using -- separator
152: ```
153: 
154: ### Permission Mode Values
155: 
156: | Value | Behavior | Best For |
157: |-------|----------|----------|
158: | `auto` | Auto-approves read-only tools; prompts for writes and shell | Review, analysis, research |
159: | `accept-edits` | Auto-approves workspace edits + read-only; prompts for shell | Code generation, bug fixing, documentation |
160: | `smart` | Auto-runs actions a fast model judges safe | Trusted workflows with judgment calls |
161: | `dangerous` | Auto-approves all tools without prompting | Full trust — **requires explicit user approval** |
162: | `autonomous` | Sandbox-enforced; only available with `--sandbox` | Unattended execution with OS-level limits |
163: 
164: ### Usage Examples
165: 
166: ```bash
167: # Interactive REPL
168: devin
169: 
170: # Non-interactive with model selection
171: devin -p --model gpt-5-6-luna-max -- "Refactor utils.ts to use async/await"
172: 
173: # With permission mode for file edits
174: devin -p --permission-mode accept-edits -- "Add error handling to auth.ts"
175: 
176: # Continue the most recent session
177: devin -c
178: 
179: # Resume a specific session
180: devin -r brisk-otter
181: 
182: # With OS-level sandbox
183: devin --sandbox -p -- "Run the test suite and fix failures"
184: 
185: # Load prompt from file
186: devin -p --prompt-file ./prompt.txt
187: 
188: # Export conversation
189: devin --export out.json -- fix the tests
190: 
191: # Start REPL with initial prompt
192: devin -- add a login page

197: ## 5. MODEL SELECTION

199: ### Supported Models
200: 
201: Devin dispatches **`swe`** (alias → `swe-2`) at the **`accept-edits`** permission mode by default. The model is switched per-dispatch with `--model <alias>` (short names resolve to the latest version in that family). There is no headless reasoning-effort flag — depth is expressed through the permission mode (autonomy) and the chosen model, not a reasoning flag; interactive REPL sessions cycle thinking depth with `Alt+T` (macOS: `Opt+T`).

203: **Full curated roster (DeepSeek / Gemini / GLM-5.2 / GPT-5.6 Luna Max / SWE-2 families) → [providers-and-models.md](./providers-and-models.md).** Devin's native Adaptive router and full 48-family roster are out of this skill's curated scope.

209: devin --model gpt-5-6-luna-max -- refactor this module
210: devin --model glm-5-2 -- explain this code

216: /model deepseek-v4-flash-max

228: | Task Type | Model | Rationale |
229: |-----------|-------|-----------|
230: | Architecture decisions | `gpt-5-6-luna-max` | Multi-faceted analysis benefits from deep reasoning |
231: | Security audits | `gpt-5-6-luna-max` | Catches subtle vulnerability patterns |
232: | Complex planning | `gpt-5-6-luna-max` / `glm-5-2-max` | Multi-strategy evaluation benefits from depth |
233: | Code generation | `glm-5-2` / `glm-5-2-max` | Balanced for most generation tasks |
234: | Standard code review | `glm-5-2` / `swe-2-high` | Efficient for pattern-based review |
235: | Implementation | `glm-5-2` / `swe-2-high` | Balanced for translating specs to code |

240: | Cost-sensitive work | `swe` / `swe-2-medium` | SWE-2 is free across all three effort tiers |

400: ## 9. CONFIGURATION FILES
401: 
402: ### Directory Structure
403: 
404: ```
405: .devin/
406: ├── config.json          # Project-level CLI configuration
407: ├── config.local.json    # Local override (not shared with team)
408: ├── hooks/               # Lifecycle hooks
409: └── agents/
410:     └── [name]/

414: ### config.json Format
415: 
416: ```json
417: // .devin/config.json or ~/.config/devin/config.json
418: {
419:   "agent": {
420:     "model": "swe"
421:   },
422:   "permissions": {
423:     "allow": [
424:       "Read(src/**)",
425:       "Write(src/**)",
426:       "Exec(git)",
427:       "Exec(npm run)"
428:     ],
429:     "deny": [
430:       "Exec(rm -rf)",
431:       "Exec(sudo)"
432:     ]
433:   },
434:   "mcpServers": {
435:     "my-server": {
436:       "command": "npx",
437:       "args": ["@company/mcp-server"],
438:       "transport": "stdio"
439:     }
440:   }
441: }
442: ```
443: 
444: ### Permission Syntax
445: 
446: **Scope-based:**
447: 
448: | Matcher | Controls | Example |
449: |---------|----------|---------|
450: | `Read(glob)` | File read access | `Read(src/**)` |
451: | `Write(glob)` | File write access | `Write(src/**)` |
452: | `Exec(prefix)` | Shell command execution | `Exec(git)`, `Exec(npm run)` |
453: | `Fetch(pattern)` | HTTP fetch access | `Fetch(https://api.github.com/*)` |
454: 
455: **Tool-based:** `read`, `edit`, `grep`, `glob`, `exec`
456: 
457: **MCP tool-based:** `mcp__server__tool`, `mcp__server__*`, `mcp__*`
458: 
459: ### Permission Precedence
460: 
461: 1. Organization/team settings (if enterprise) — highest
462: 2. Session-level grants (interactive approvals)
463: 3. Project local config (`.devin/config.local.json`)
464: 4. Project config (`.devin/config.json`)
465: 5. User config (`~/.config/devin/config.json`) — lowest
466: 
467: Deny is checked before ask, and ask is checked before allow. A deny rule always wins.

471: ## 10. PERMISSION MODES
472: 
473: Permission modes control what the agent can do without asking for approval. Always choose the least-permissive mode that allows the task to complete.
474: 
475: ### Mode Reference
476: 
477: | Mode | Flag | Read-only | Fetch | Bash | File edits | Use Case |
478: |------|------|-----------|-------|------|------------|----------|
479: | **Auto** | `auto` | Auto | Prompt | Prompt | Prompt | Analysis, review, exploration |
480: | **Accept Edits** | `accept-edits` | Auto | Prompt | Prompt | Auto (workspace) | Code generation, refactoring |
481: | **Smart** | `smart` | Auto | Safe actions | Safe actions | Auto (workspace) | Trusted workflows with judgment |
482: | **Dangerous** | `dangerous` | Auto | Auto | Auto | Auto | Full trust — **requires explicit approval** |
483: | **Autonomous** | `autonomous` (+ `--sandbox`) | Auto | Auto (sandbox) | Auto (sandbox) | Prompt (edit/write tools bypass sandbox) | Unattended execution with OS limits |
484: 
485: ### Safety Guidance
486: 
487: ```bash
488: # SAFE: Auto mode for analysis
489: devin -p --permission-mode auto --model swe -- "Map the authentication flow"
490: 
491: # STANDARD: Accept Edits for code changes
492: devin -p --permission-mode accept-edits --model swe -- "Add error handling to all API routes"
493: 
494: # ELEVATED RISK: Dangerous mode — use only with explicit approval
495: devin -p --permission-mode dangerous --model gpt-5-6-luna-max -- "Migrate database schema"
496: 
497: # AUTONOMOUS: OS-enforced sandbox
498: devin --sandbox -p --model swe -- "Run the test suite and fix failures"
499: ```
500: 
501: ### Bypass vs Autonomous
502: 
503: | | Bypass (`dangerous`) | Autonomous (`--sandbox`) |
504: |---|---|---|
505: | Requires `--sandbox` | No | Yes (only available in sandbox sessions) |
506: | Shell commands | Auto-approved, unrestricted | Auto-approved, contained by sandbox |
507: | File writes via edit/write tools | Auto-approved anywhere | Still prompt (granting a scope expands the sandbox) |
508: | Network access | Unrestricted | Filtered by sandbox domain allow/deny lists |
509: | Respects admin Team Settings | Yes | Yes |
510: 
511: Pick `dangerous` when you trust the agent with your whole machine. Pick `--sandbox` (autonomous) when you want unattended execution with OS-enforced limits.

16: # Devin Cloud Handoff Reference
17: 
18: Complete reference for the `/handoff` command and cloud Devin session mechanics.
19: 
20: ---
21: 
22: ## 1. OVERVIEW
23: 
24: ### Core Principle
25: 
26: When a task outgrows the local terminal — or you want Devin to keep working while you step away — the `/handoff` command transfers the current session to a cloud Devin session. The cloud session gets its own VM with a shell, browser, and full repo access, so it can keep going after you close your laptop.
27: 
28: ### Purpose
29: 
30: Documents the `/handoff` command mechanics, use cases, state transfer, and integration patterns for offloading work from the local Devin CLI to a cloud Devin session.
31: 
32: ### When to Use
33: 
34: - **VM or server tasks** — running a dev server, hitting endpoints, Docker builds
35: - **Browser-dependent workflows** — screenshots, OAuth flows, end-to-end tests, scraping
36: - **CI/CD** — pipeline debugging, deployments, infrastructure changes
37: - **Long-running work** — migrations, batch jobs, large refactors
38: - **Parallel execution** — offload work to the cloud while you keep coding locally
39: 
40: ### When NOT to Use
41: 
42: - Quick edits that complete faster locally
43: - Tasks requiring interactive approval prompts (cloud sessions are less interactive)
44: - Tasks involving sensitive data without confirming cloud session isolation
45: - Tasks where the local environment has specific dependencies not available in the cloud VM
46: 
47: ---
48: 
49: ## 2. HANDOFF MECHANICS
50: 
51: ### The /handoff Command
52: 
53: The `/handoff` command is available inside an interactive Devin REPL session. It packages the conversation context and current git branch, then creates a cloud session that picks up where you left off.
54: 
55: **Basic usage:**
56: 
57: ```
58: /handoff fix the flaky integration tests in CI
59: ```
60: 
61: **Without a task description:**
62: 
63: ```
64: /handoff
65: ```
66: 
67: Running `/handoff` without a task description makes the cloud session continue from where you left off automatically.
68: 
69: ### What Carries Over
70: 
71: The cloud session starts in a fresh VM, so the CLI includes everything it needs to pick up the thread:
72: 
73: | What | Details |
74: |------|---------|
75: | **Repo and branch** | The cloud session clones the right repo and checks out the branch you're on |
76: | **Conversation context** | What you and Devin have been working on in the current session |
77: | **Uncommitted changes** | Your work-in-progress diff carries over. Commit or stash anything you don't want sent |
78: 
79: ### What Does NOT Carry Over
80: 
81: - Local environment variables not in the repo
82: - Locally installed tools or dependencies not defined in the repo
83: - Active MCP server connections (must be re-established in the cloud session)
84: - Local file system state outside the repo
85: 
86: ### Tracking Progress
87: 
88: After handoff, track the cloud session's progress from:
89: 
90: 1. **Your terminal** — the CLI shows the cloud session status
91: 2. **The Devin web app** — `https://app.devin.ai` provides a full cloud session dashboard
92: 
93: ---
94: 
95: ## 3. USE CASES
96: 
97: ### Long-Running Tasks
98: 
99: Tasks that would tie up a local terminal for an extended period are ideal for cloud handoff. The cloud VM runs independently — you can close your laptop and check back later.
100: 
101: ```
102: /handoff run the full integration test suite, fix any failures, and verify the build passes
103: ```
104: 
105: **Best for:** migrations, batch jobs, large refactors, full test suite runs.
106: 
107: ### Complex Refactors
108: 
109: Multi-file refactors that require deep reasoning and many tool calls benefit from the cloud session's dedicated resources.
110: 
111: ```
112: /handoff refactor the entire authentication module to use a strategy pattern with pluggable providers
113: ```
114: 
115: **Best for:** architectural changes, dependency upgrades, framework migrations.
116: 
117: ### CI-Like Validation
118: 
119: Run validation pipelines in the cloud that mirror CI behavior — build, test, lint, type-check.
120: 
121: ```
122: /handoff run the full CI pipeline locally: lint, type-check, unit tests, integration tests, and e2e tests. Fix any failures and report the results.
123: ```
124: 
125: **Best for:** pre-PR validation, release readiness checks, pipeline debugging.
126: 
127: ### Browser-Dependent Workflows
128: 
129: The cloud session includes a browser, enabling workflows that are impossible in a pure terminal:
130: 
131: ```
132: /handoff test the OAuth flow end-to-end: start the dev server, navigate to the login page, complete the OAuth flow, and verify the callback handles the token correctly
133: ```
134: 
135: **Best for:** OAuth flow testing, E2E test runs, web scraping, screenshot verification.
136: 
137: ### Parallel Execution
138: 
139: Offload work to the cloud while you continue coding locally. The cloud session runs independently.
140: 
141: ```
142: # In your local session:
143: /handoff generate comprehensive integration tests for the API layer
144: 
145: # Meanwhile, you continue working on the frontend locally
146: ```
147: 
148: **Best for:** generating tests while implementing features, running background validation while coding, parallel task decomposition.
149: 
150: ---
151: 
152: ## 4. STATE TRANSFER
153: 
154: ### Git State
155: 
156: The handoff transfers the current git branch and uncommitted changes. The cloud session:
157: 
158: 1. Clones the repository
159: 2. Checks out the branch you were on
160: 3. Applies your uncommitted work-in-progress diff
161: 
162: **Important:** Commit or stash anything you do NOT want sent to the cloud. The handoff transfers the working tree as-is.
163: 
164: ### Conversation Context
165: 
166: The full conversation context from the current session is packaged and sent to the cloud session. This includes:
167: 
168: - All user messages and Devin's responses
169: - Tool calls and their results
170: - Any decisions made during the session
171: - The current task state and progress
172: 
173: The cloud session picks up the thread as if you had never closed your local terminal.
174: 
175: ### Environment Setup
176: 
177: The cloud VM is a fresh environment. Any environment-specific setup must be defined in the repo (via a `environment.yaml` or similar) or re-established in the cloud session.
178: 
179: For reproducible cloud environments, use Declarative Repo Setup (DRS):
180: 
181: ```bash
182: # Manage environment blueprints

280:

284: | **Browser needed** | No | Yes |
285: | **VM/server needed** | No | Yes (dev server, Docker, endpoints) |
286: | **Interactive approval** | Yes (can prompt) | Limited (cloud runs more autonomously) |
287: | **Laptop must stay open** | Yes (process tied to terminal) | No (runs independently) |
288: | **Parallel work** | Blocks local terminal | Frees local terminal |
289: | **CI-like validation** | Limited (local environment) | Full VM with CI-like setup |
290: | **Cost** | Local compute only | Cloud session usage |
291: | **Network access** | Local network | Cloud VM network |

334: - **Have a rollback plan** — know how to revert if the cloud session makes unwanted changes

442: ## 12. MEMORY EPILOGUE
443: 
444: ### Purpose
445: 
446: Append this epilogue to any delegated prompt when the calling AI needs structured session memory back from Devin CLI. The agent will include the delimited section in its output, enabling the calling AI to extract, parse, and save it via `generate-context.js`.
447: 
448: ### Epilogue Template
449: 
450: Append the following text to the end of any Devin CLI prompt:
451: 
452: ```text
453: When you finish, include a session memory section in your output using EXACTLY this format:
454: 
455: <!-- MEMORY_HANDBACK_START -->
456: ## Session Memory
457: 
458: ### Summary
459: [1-3 sentences: what was accomplished]
460: 
461: ### Files Modified
462: - path/to/file.ts
463: 
464: ### Decisions
465: - Decision and rationale
466: 
467: ### Next Steps
468: - Remaining work
469: 
470: ### Spec Folder
471: [spec-folder-name]
472: <!-- MEMORY_HANDBACK_END -->
473: ```
474: 
475: ### Extraction by Calling AI
476: 
477: After receiving agent output, the calling AI extracts the handback section:
478: 
479: ```javascript
480: const match = output.match(/<!-- MEMORY_HANDBACK_START -->([\s\S]*?)<!-- MEMORY_HANDBACK_END -->/);
481: ```
482: 
483: Then constructs structured JSON and saves via:
484: 
485: ```bash
486: # Redact or scrub secrets before writing the JSON payload
487: # Write extracted data to JSON
488: cat > /tmp/save-context-data.json << 'JSONEOF'
489: {
490:   "specFolder": "<extracted or provided by calling AI>",
491:   "user_prompts": [
492:     "<delegated task or user goal>"
493:   ],
494:   "observations": [
495:     {
496:       "type": "implementation",
497:       "title": "<short accomplishment>",
498:       "narrative": "<what changed and why it matters>",
499:       "facts": [
500:         "<verification or durable implementation detail>"
501:       ]
502:     }
503:   ],
504:   "recent_context": [
505:     {
506:       "request": "<delegated task or user goal>",
507:       "learning": "<durable implementation detail or verification result>"
508:     }
509:   ],
510:   "FILES": [
511:     {
512:       "FILE_PATH": "<extracted path when known>",
513:       "DESCRIPTION": "<what changed and why it matters>",
514:       "ACTION": "Modified",
515:       "MODIFICATION_MAGNITUDE": "small",
516:       "_provenance": "tool"
517:     }
518:   ],
519:   "sessionSummary": "<extracted summary>",
520:   "keyDecisions": ["<extracted decisions>"],
521:   "nextSteps": ["<extracted remaining work>"],
522:   "triggerPhrases": ["<auto-derived from task>"]
523: }
524: JSONEOF
525: 
526: # Save via generate-context.js JSON mode
527: node .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/dist/continuity/generate-context.js /tmp/save-context-data.json [spec-folder]
528: ```
529: 
530: Structured JSON is the required save path. You can pass the payload via temp file, `--stdin`, or `--json`. Do not call `generate-context.js` with only a spec folder.

95:   --model adaptive --permission-mode accept-edits
96: ```

99: 
100: ## 3. CODE REVIEW
101: 
102: ### Comprehensive Review
103: 
104: Framework: TIDD-EC
105: 
106: Full code review covering correctness, style, maintainability, and performance.
107: 
108: ```bash
109: devin -p "Review the file at [file-path] thoroughly. Check for: 1) Logic errors and edge cases, 2) Code style and naming consistency, 3) Error handling completeness, 4) Performance issues, 5) Maintainability concerns. For each issue found, provide the line reference, severity (critical/warning/info), and a suggested fix." \
110:   --model opus --permission-mode auto
111: ```
112: 
113: ### Security-Focused Review
114: 
115: Framework: TIDD-EC
116: 
117: Review focused on security vulnerabilities and attack surfaces.
118: 
119: ```bash
120: devin -p "Perform a security audit of [file-path]. Check for: 1) Injection vulnerabilities (SQL, XSS, command injection), 2) Authentication and authorization flaws, 3) Sensitive data exposure (hardcoded secrets, logging PII), 4) Input validation gaps, 5) Insecure dependencies or patterns, 6) eval() or dynamic code execution. Rate each finding as critical/high/medium/low severity." \
121:   --model opus --permission-mode auto
122: ```
123: 
124: ### Subagent-Delegated Review
125: 
126: Framework: TIDD-EC
127: 
128: Use a subagent for parallel review work.
129: 
130: ```bash
131: devin -p "Use a subagent_explore subagent to review [file-path] for code quality issues. The subagent should check for logic errors, style issues, and missing error handling. Report findings with severity ratings." \
132:   --model adaptive --permission-mode auto
133: ```
134: 
135: ---
136: 
137: ## 4. BUG FIXING
138: 
139: ### Fix Identified Bugs
140: 
141: Framework: RCAF + TIDD-EC
142: 
143: Fix a known bug with description and reproduction context.
144: 
145: ```bash
146: devin -p "Fix this bug in [file-path]: [description]. The expected behavior is [requirements]. The actual behavior is [description]. Apply the minimal fix without refactoring unrelated code. Explain the root cause and the fix. Start immediately." \
147:   --model adaptive --permission-mode accept-edits
148: ```
149: 
150: ### Auto-Detect and Fix
151: 
152: Framework: RCAF + TIDD-EC
153: 
154: Let Devin scan a file for potential bugs and apply fixes.
155: 
156: ```bash
157: devin -p "Scan [file-path] for bugs. Look for: null/undefined access, off-by-one errors, race conditions, unhandled promise rejections, incorrect type coercions, resource leaks, and logic errors. For each bug found: describe the issue, show the fix, and explain why it is a bug. Apply all fixes. Start immediately." \
158:   --model adaptive --permission-mode accept-edits
159: ```
160: 
161: ### Subagent-Delegated Debugging
162: 
163: Framework: RCAF + TIDD-EC
164: 
165: Use a general subagent for fresh-perspective debugging.
166: 
167: ```bash
168: devin -p "Use a subagent_general subagent to debug this issue: [description]. The error occurs at [file-path]:[line]. Prior attempts: [what was tried]. The subagent should apply the minimal fix and report what was changed." \
169:   --model adaptive --permission-mode accept-edits
170: ```
171: 
172: ---
173: 
174: ## 5. TEST GENERATION
175: 
176: ### Unit Tests
177: 
178: Framework: RCAF
179: 
180: Generate unit tests for a specific file or module.
181: 
182: ```bash
183: devin -p "Generate comprehensive [framework] unit tests for [file-path]. Cover: 1) Happy path for each exported function, 2) Edge cases (empty input, null, boundary values), 3) Error conditions and thrown exceptions, 4) Mock external dependencies. Use describe/it blocks with descriptive names. Output a complete test file." \
184:   --model adaptive --permission-mode accept-edits
185: ```
186: 
187: **Example (Jest):**
188: 
189: ```bash
190: devin -p "Generate comprehensive Jest unit tests for src/utils/validator.ts. Cover: 1) Happy path for each exported function, 2) Edge cases (empty input, null, boundary values), 3) Error conditions and thrown exceptions, 4) Mock external dependencies. Use describe/it blocks with descriptive names. Output a complete test file." \
191:   --model adaptive --permission-mode accept-edits
192: ```
193: 
194: ### Integration Tests
195: 
196: Framework: RCAF
197: 
198: Generate integration tests that test multiple components working together.
199: 
200: ```bash
201: devin -p "Generate [framework] integration tests for the [description] workflow. Test files involved: [file-path]. Cover: 1) End-to-end happy path, 2) Error propagation across layers, 3) Database/API interaction patterns, 4) Setup and teardown for test isolation. Write the complete test file." \
202:   --model adaptive --permission-mode accept-edits
203: ```
204: 
205: ### Test Coverage Analysis
206: 
207: Framework: RCAF
208: 
209: Identify missing test coverage in an existing test suite.
210: 
211: ```bash
212: devin -p "Analyze [test-file] against the implementation in [source-file]. Identify: 1) Functions with no test coverage, 2) Edge cases not covered by existing tests, 3) Error paths not exercised. List gaps by priority (critical/high/medium) and suggest specific test cases to add." \
213:   --model adaptive --permission-mode auto
214: ```
215: 
216: ---
217: 
218: ## 6. SUBAGENT DELEGATION
219: 
220: ### Parallel Research with Explore Subagents
221: 
222: Framework: CRAFT
223: 
224: Spawn multiple explore subagents for independent research tasks.
225: 
226: ```bash
227: devin -p "Spawn [N] subagent_explore subagents in the background: [task-1], [task-2], [task-3]. When all complete, synthesize a summary of the findings." \
228:   --model adaptive --permission-mode auto
229: ```
230: 
231: **Example:**
232: 
233: ```bash
234: devin -p "Spawn three subagent_explore subagents in the background: 1. Map the API layer — list all endpoints and handlers, 2. Map the database layer — list all models and relationships, 3. Map the auth layer — trace the authentication flow. When all three complete, synthesize an architecture summary." \
235:   --model adaptive --permission-mode auto
236: ```
237: 
238: ### Code Changes with General Subagent
239: 
240: Framework: RCAF
241: 
242: Use a general subagent for focused code changes.
243: 
244: ```bash
245: devin -p "Use a subagent_general subagent to [description]. Apply the changes and report what was modified and why." \
246:   --model adaptive --permission-mode accept-edits
247: ```
248: 
249: ### Custom Subagent Profile
250: 
251: Framework: RCAF
252: 
253: Use a custom AGENT.md profile for specialized work.
254: 
255: ```bash
256: devin -p "Use the [profile-name] subagent to [description]. Report the results." \
257:   --model adaptive --permission-mode auto
258: ```
259: 
260: ---
261: 
262: ## 7. CLOUD HANDOFF
263: 
264: ### Long-Running Task Handoff
265: 
266: Framework: CRAFT
267: 
268: Hand off a long-running task to a cloud Devin session.
269: 
270: ```bash
271: # Start a session, then hand off inside the REPL
272: devin -- "[description of long-running task]" --permission-mode accept-edits
273: # Inside the REPL:
274: /handoff [task description]
275: ```
276: 
277: **Example:**
278: 
279: ```bash
280: devin -- "Run the full integration test suite, fix any failures, and verify the build passes" --permission-mode accept-edits
281: # Inside the REPL:
282: /handoff run the full integration test suite, fix any failures, and verify the build passes
283: ```
284: 
285: ### Browser-Dependent Workflow Handoff
286: 
287: Framework: CRAFT
288: 
289: Hand off a task that needs a browser to the cloud.
290: 
291: ```bash
292: devin -- "Test the OAuth flow end-to-end: start the dev server, navigate to the login page, complete the OAuth flow, and verify the callback handles the token correctly" --permission-mode accept-edits
293: # Inside the REPL:
294: /handoff test the OAuth flow end-to-end
295: ```
296: 
297: ---
298: 
299: ## 8. ARCHITECTURE ANALYSIS
300: 
301: ### Project Analysis
302: 
303: Framework: CRAFT
304: 
305: Analyze overall project architecture and structure.
306: 
307: ```bash
308: devin -p "Analyze the project structure in [directory]. Provide: 1) High-level architecture overview, 2) Key modules and their responsibilities, 3) Dependency relationships between major components, 4) Entry points and data flow, 5) Technology stack summary. Output as structured markdown." \
309:   --model opus --permission-mode auto
310: ```
311: 
312: ### Dependency Analysis
313: 
314: Framework: CRAFT
315: 
316: Map dependencies and identify coupling issues.
317: 
318: ```bash
319: devin -p "Analyze dependencies in [directory]. Identify: 1) Direct and transitive dependency chains, 2) Circular dependencies, 3) Tightly coupled modules, 4) Unused imports or dead code paths, 5) Dependency inversion violations. Suggest concrete decoupling strategies." \
320:   --model opus --permission-mode auto
321: ```
322: 
323: ---
324: 
325: ## 9. SPECIALIZED TASKS
326: 
327: ### Git Commit Message
328: 
329: Framework: RCAF
330: 
331: Generate a commit message from staged changes.
332: 
333: ```bash
334: devin -p "Based on the following git diff, write a commit message following Conventional Commits format (type(scope): description). Include a body explaining why the change was made. Diff: $(git diff --cached)" \
335:   --model adaptive --permission-mode auto
336: ```
337: 
338: ### Code Explanation
339: 
340: Framework: CRAFT
341: 
342: Get a detailed explanation of unfamiliar code.
343: 
344: ```bash
345: devin -p "Explain [file-path] in detail. Cover: 1) What the code does at a high level, 2) Key algorithms or patterns used, 3) How data flows through the functions, 4) Why certain design decisions were likely made, 5) Any non-obvious behavior or gotchas. Write for a developer unfamiliar with this codebase." \
346:   --model adaptive --permission-mode auto
347: ```
348: 
349: ### Error Diagnosis
350: 
351: Framework: TIDD-EC
352: 
353: Diagnose an error message with full context.
354: 
355: ```bash
356: devin -p "Diagnose this error: [error message]. It occurs when running [description] in [file-path]. Stack trace: [stack trace]. Provide: 1) Root cause analysis, 2) Step-by-step fix, 3) How to prevent this error in the future." \
357:   --model adaptive --permission-mode accept-edits
358: ```
359: 
360: ### Session-Based Multi-Step Task
361: 
362: Framework: CRAFT
363: 
364: Orchestrate a complex multi-step task across sessions.
365: 
366: ```bash
367: # Step 1: Begin task
368: devin -p "Begin implementing [feature]. Start with the interface design and data model. Stop before writing implementation. Describe the planned approach." \
369:   --model adaptive --permission-mode accept-edits
370: 
371: # Step 2: Continue and implement
372: devin -c -p "Continue implementing [feature] from where we left off. Implement the core logic." \
373:   --model adaptive --permission-mode accept-edits
374: ```
375: 
376: ### Research-Then-Implement
377: 
378: Framework: CRISPE + RCAF
379: 
380: Research best practices, then apply them to the codebase.
381: 
382: ```bash
383: # Phase 1: Research
384: devin -p "Research current best practices for [topic] in [language/framework]. Summarize the top 3 recommended approaches with pros and cons." \
385:   --model adaptive --permission-mode auto
386: 
387: # Phase 2: Implement
388: devin -p "Based on best practices for [topic], implement [description] in [file-path]. Use the [approach] pattern. Preserve all existing behavior." \
389:   --model adaptive --permission-mode accept-edits
390: ```
391: 
392: ---
393: 
394: ## 10. TEMPLATE VARIABLES
395: 
396: All placeholders used across templates in this file:
397: 
398: | Variable | Description | Example Values |
399: |----------|-------------|----------------|
400: | `[file]` | Relative file path | `src/utils/validator.ts`, `lib/api.py` |
401: | `[file-path]` | Full file path for Devin dispatch | `src/auth/handler.ts` |
402: | `[directory]` | Project or module directory | `./src/`, `./packages/core/` |
403: | `[description]` | Free-text description of intent or behavior | `"rate-limiting middleware"`, `"Cannot read property of null"` |
404: | `[features]` | List of features or capabilities | `"auth, logging, caching"` |
405: | `[requirements]` | Specific requirements or constraints | `"must handle 1000 req/s"`, `"readability and testability"` |
406: | `[framework]` | Framework name | `React`, `Vue`, `Express`, `FastAPI`, `Jest`, `Vitest` |
407: | `[language]` | Programming language | `TypeScript`, `Python`, `Go`, `Rust` |
408: | `[format]` | Code format or structure type | `module`, `class`, `component`, `middleware` |
409: | `[topic]` | Research subject or technology name | `Next.js 15`, `Bun vs Deno`, `React Server Components` |
410: | `[error message]` | Verbatim error text | `"Cannot read properties of undefined"` |
411: | `[stack trace]` | Error stack trace | Multi-line stack trace text |
412: | `[N]` | Number of subagents | `3`, `5` |
413: | `[task-N]` | Subagent task description | `"Map the API layer"` |
414: | `[profile-name]` | Custom subagent profile name | `reviewer`, `test-runner` |
415: | `[session-id]` | Devin session identifier | `brisk-otter` |
416: 
417: ### Placeholder Conventions
418: 
419: - **Single value**: `[file]` - replace with one value
420: - **List value**: `[features]` - replace with comma-separated list
421: - **Free text**: `[description]` - replace with natural language
422: - **Compound**: Some templates use the same placeholder multiple times. Replace each occurrence independently.
423: 
424: ---
425: 
426: ## 11. RELATED RESOURCES
427: 
428: ### Parent
429: 
430: - [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md) - Main skill instructions and invocation patterns
431: 
432: ### References
433: 
434: - [cli-reference.md](../references/cli-reference.md) - Complete CLI subcommand and flag reference
435: - [integration-patterns.md](../references/integration-patterns.md) - Cross-AI orchestration patterns
436: - [devin-tools.md](../references/devin-tools.md) - Built-in capabilities (run_subagent, /handoff, MCP, session management)
437: - [agent-delegation.md](../references/agent-delegation.md) - Subagent profile roster and custom AGENT.md patterns
438: - [cloud-handoff.md](../references/cloud-handoff.md) - /handoff cloud-handoff mechanics and state transfer
439: 
440: ---
441: 
442: ## 12. MEMORY EPILOGUE
443: 
444: ### Purpose
445: 
446: Append this epilogue to any delegated prompt when the calling AI needs structured session memory back from Devin CLI. The agent will include the delimited section in its output, enabling the calling AI to extract, parse, and save it via `generate-context.js`.
447: 
448: ### Epilogue Template
449: 
450: Append the following text to the end of any Devin CLI prompt:
451: 
452: ```text
453: When you finish, include a session memory section in your output using EXACTLY this format:
454: 
455: <!-- MEMORY_HANDBACK_START -->
456: ## Session Memory
457: 
458: ### Summary
459: [1-3 sentences: what was accomplished]
460: 
461: ### Files Modified
462: - path/to/file.ts
463: 
464: ### Decisions
465: - Decision and rationale
466: 
467: ### Next Steps
468: - Remaining work
469: 
470: ### Spec Folder
471: [spec-folder-name]
472: <!-- MEMORY_HANDBACK_END -->
473: ```
474: 
475: ### Extraction by Calling AI
476: 
477: After receiving agent output, the calling AI extracts the handback section:
478: 
479: ```javascript
480: const match = output.match(/<!-- MEMORY_HANDBACK_START -->([\s\S]*?)<!-- MEMORY_HANDBACK_END -->/);
481: ```
482: 
483: Then constructs structured JSON and saves via:
484: 
485: ```bash
486: # Redact or scrub secrets before writing the JSON payload
487: # Write extracted data to JSON
488: cat > /tmp/save-context-data.json << 'JSONEOF'
489: {
490:   "specFolder": "<extracted or provided by calling AI>",
491:   "user_prompts": [
492:     "<delegated task or user goal>"
493:   ],
494:   "observations": [
495:     {
496:       "type": "implementation",
497:       "title": "<short accomplishment>",
498:       "narrative": "<what changed and why it matters>",
499:       "facts": [
500:         "<verification or durable implementation detail>"
501:       ]
502:     }
503:   ],
504:   "recent_context": [
505:     {
506:       "request": "<delegated task or user goal>",
507:       "learning": "<durable implementation detail or verification result>"
508:     }
509:   ],
510:   "FILES": [
511:     {
512:       "FILE_PATH": "<extracted path when known>",
513:       "DESCRIPTION": "<what changed and why it matters>",
514:       "ACTION": "Modified",
515:       "MODIFICATION_MAGNITUDE": "small",
516:       "_provenance": "tool"
517:     }
518:   ],
519:   "sessionSummary": "<extracted summary>",
520:   "keyDecisions": ["<extracted decisions>"],
521:   "nextSteps": ["<extracted remaining work>"],
522:   "triggerPhrases": ["<auto-derived from task>"]
523: }
524: JSONEOF
525: 
526: # Save via generate-context.js JSON mode
527: node .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/dist/continuity/generate-context.js /tmp/save-context-data.json [spec-folder]
528: ```
529: 
530: Structured JSON is the required save path. You can pass the payload via temp file, `--stdin`, or `--json`. Do not call `generate-context.js` with only a spec folder.
531: 
532: ---
533: 
534: ## 13. MODEL SELECTION FOR TEMPLATES
535: 
536: All templates default to `--model adaptive`. Tune the model to the task.
537: 
538: ### Deep Reasoning (architecture, security, planning)
539: 
540: ```bash
541: # Architecture analysis with Opus
542: devin -p "Analyze the architecture of this project. Identify coupling issues, circular dependencies, and scalability concerns." \
543:   --model opus --permission-mode auto
544: 
545: # Security audit with Opus
546: devin -p "Perform a thorough security audit of [file-path]. Check OWASP Top 10, auth bypasses, injection vectors, and cryptographic weaknesses." \
547:   --model opus --permission-mode auto
548: ```
549: 
550: ### Quick Edits (cost-sensitive)
551: 
552: ```bash
553: # Quick fix with SWE Fast
554: devin -p "Fix the typo in the error message at line 42 in [file-path]." \
555:   --model swe-1-6-fast --permission-mode accept-edits
556: 
557: # Quick lookup with SWE
558: devin -p "List all TODO comments in src/." \
559:   --model swe --permission-mode auto
560: ```
561: 
562: ### Mixed Effort Workflow
563: 
564: Use `opus` for analysis, then `adaptive` for implementation:
565: 
566: ```bash
567: # Step 1: Deep analysis with Opus
568: devin -p "Identify all security vulnerabilities in src/auth/" \
569:   --model opus --permission-mode auto > /tmp/security-findings.txt
570: 
571: # Step 2: Fix with Adaptive
572: devin -p "Fix these security issues: $(cat /tmp/security-findings.txt)" \
573:   --model adaptive --permission-mode accept-edits
574: ```

# Shared Smart-Router Helpers (cli-* family)

Use this reference when implementing shared helpers in a cli-* router.

---

## 1. OVERVIEW

### Purpose

Canonical helper-function bodies (_task_text, _guard_in_skill, discover_markdown_resources, score_intents, select_intents, route_<provider>_resources) shared across the seven cli-* sibling skills. Each cli-* skill provides its own INTENT_SIGNALS, RESOURCE_MAP, LOADING_LEVELS, UNKNOWN_FALLBACK_CHECKLIST inline.

### When to Use

- Use when implementing or reviewing cli-* routing helpers.

None of the seven packet `SKILL.md` files defines `_task_text()`, `_guard_in_skill()`, `discover_markdown_resources()`, `keyword_present()`, `score_intents()`, `select_intents()` or `get_routing_key()`. Every packet names `discover_markdown_resources()` and `_guard_in_skill()`. Only `cli-hermes` names `score_intents()` and `select_intents()`, while `cli-hermes` and `cli-opencode` name `load_if_available()` and `get_routing_key()`.

---

## 2. HELPER FUNCTIONS

> Pattern: see [sk-doc smart-router resilience template](../../../sk-doc/sk-create-skill/assets/skill/skill-smart-router.md).

```python
import re
from pathlib import Path

SKILL_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
RESOURCE_BASES = (SKILL_ROOT / "references", SKILL_ROOT / "assets")
DEFAULT_RESOURCE = "references/cli-reference.md"

def _task_text(task) -> str:
    return " ".join([
        str(getattr(task, "text", "")),
        str(getattr(task, "query", "")),
        " ".join(getattr(task, "keywords", []) or []),
    ]).lower()

def _guard_in_skill(relative_path: str) -> str:
    resolved = (SKILL_ROOT / relative_path).resolve()
    resolved.relative_to(SKILL_ROOT)
    if resolved.suffix.lower() != ".md":
        raise ValueError(f"Only markdown resources are routable: {relative_path}")
    return resolved.relative_to(SKILL_ROOT).as_posix()
